labels.label: def:egf

hypotheses.paper: S a Riemannian manifold endowed with its volume measure lambda (main.tex:217)
hypotheses.note: any MeasurableSpace S and any Measure lam (not assumed finite, not sigma-finite). Mathlib at the pin has no Riemannian volume (the reading the dispatch prescribes).

measurable equivalences Phi i : S ≃ᵐ S preserving the lam-null sets both ways (field IsEGFErgodic.nonsingular: lam.map (Phi i) ≪ lam ∧ lam.map (Phi i).symm ≪ lam), the measure-theoretic property a diffeomorphism has for the volume (C-6's hypothesis and its inverse). Automatic, proved: C^n diffeomorphisms (n ≥ 1) of a finite-dimensional real space with any Haar measure (EGF.nonsingular_of_diffeomorph; there IsEGFErgodic reduces to policy + group ergodicity, EGF.isEGFErgodic_diffeomorph_iff), measure-preserving moves (EGF.nonsingular_of_measurePreserving), affine maps of tori (EGF.nonsingular_torusAffineME), rotations of spheres (EGF.nonsingular_rotME). For a general Riemannian manifold the fact is standard and not formalizable at the pin. The field is needed for the generator form of C-26's 'that is' to equal the group form (EGF.FourCycle.isGroupErgodic_not_forall).

hypotheses.paper: pi(s) = sum_i alpha^i(s) delta_{Phi_i(s)} for some policy alpha : S -> [0,1]^p; an EGF is a generative flow (main.tex:217-219)
hypotheses.note: field policy : IsEGFPolicy F.policy (fun i => Phi i) alpha with F : GenerativeFlow S; with C-27 (adopted): alpha measurable, alpha^i ≥ 0, sum_i alpha^i = 1 (hence alpha^i ≤ 1). Weights are not required positive, as printed.

hypotheses.paper: the group generated by the Phi_i is ergodic for lambda (DEC-146, C-26's corrected text, replacing 'topologically ergodic', main.tex:219-221)
hypotheses.note: field ergodic : IsGroupErgodic lam (egfGroup Phi), egfGroup Phi = Subgroup.closure of the Phi_i in Equiv.Perm S (the same group as the group of diffeomorphisms they generate, acting the same way). C-26's 'that is' (every measurable A with lam(Phi_i^{-1}(A) Δ A) = 0 for all i has lam(A) = 0 or lam(S \ A) = 0) is EGF.isEGFErgodic_iff_symmDiff, word for word, through EGF.isGroupErgodic_egfGroup_iff.

findings: main.tex:219-221 (C-26, proved): topological ergodicity does not give the measure ergodicity of DEC-146, in the generalized setting. A rotation a of infinite order of AddCircle T is topologically ergodic in the printed forward-word sense (EGF.isTopologicallyErgodic_addLeft, from the density of the forward orbit EGF.denseRange_nsmul_of_addOrderOf_eq_zero; Mathlib has only the Z-orbit), so the flow (delta_{a+.}, vol) is an EGF in the printed sense (EGF.IsEGF, hence also the group reading), and its move is nonsingular both ways for the finite measure lambda = vol + sum_n 2^{-e(n)} delta_{n a} (e = Equiv.intEquivNat : Z ≃ N, EGF.orbitWeight); for that lambda the orbit Z a is an invariant set of positive measure (its atoms) and co-measure >= vol(S) > 0, so it is not an EGF in DEC-146's sense (EGF.isEGF_not_isEGFErgodic; instance a = sqrt 2 on R/Z, EGF.isEGF_not_isEGFErgodic_sqrt_two). This lambda is not the volume: for the volume the same rotation is an EGF (EGF.isEGFErgodic_circleRotFlow_iff). In the paper's exact setting (a smooth volume) the witness would be a minimal diffeomorphism not ergodic for the volume (Furstenberg 1961, on T^2), not formalized.

main.tex:219-221 (C-26, proved, converse): DEC-146's ergodicity does not give topological ergodicity in either printed reading: on Bool with lambda = delta_true the identity flow is an EGF in DEC-146's sense (every group is ergodic for a Dirac mass, EGF.isGroupErgodic_dirac) while the identity is topologically ergodic neither with forward words nor with the group (EGF.isEGFErgodic_not_isEGF). The measure is not of full support, unlike a Riemannian volume; with a full-support lambda an ergodic action still need not have every orbit dense (a fixed point of measure zero), which is not formalized here.

C-26's corrected text (the 'That is' sentence) states the generator form, lambda(Phi_i^{-1}(A) Δ A) = 0 for all i; it equals ergodicity of the generated group as soon as the moves are nonsingular both ways (EGF.isGroupErgodic_egfGroup_iff, via EGF.ae_invariant_of_mem_closure_of_quasi), automatic for diffeomorphisms and the volume. Without nonsingularity the two differ: the rotation of Fin 4 with lambda = delta_0 + delta_2 generates a group ergodic for lambda while {0, 1} is a.e.-invariant under the rotation with measure 1 and co-measure 1 (EGF.FourCycle.isGroupErgodic_not_forall). The generator form always implies the group form (EGF.isGroupErgodic_egfGroup_of_forall).

DEC-146's clause is exactly the hypothesis of the universality theorems in their C-29 form: for an EGF policy with positive weights (main.tex:288's softmax head) and nonsingular moves whose kernel has a finite invariant lambda-hat ~ lambda, lambda finite, the flow is an EGF in DEC-146's sense iff its policy is universal (EGF.isEGFErgodic_iff_isUniversalPolicy); with positive weights the clause is the ergodicity of the kernel (EGF.isEGFErgodic_iff_isKernelErgodic). For measure-preserving moves, finite lambda and the uniform policy, a family of uniform-kernel flows with outflows ≪ lambda containing (pi, f lambda) for f in a set dense in the non-negative cone of L2(lambda) is epsilon-universal iff the generated group is ergodic (EGF.universality_of_isEGFErgodic) iff each member is an EGF (EGF.isUniversalFamilyEps_iff_forall_isEGFErgodic); sufficiency needs no restriction on the family (EGF.isUniversalFamilyEps_of_isGroupErgodic). So l.238's 'Ergodicity guarantees ... flow-matching' holds in the epsilon form with DEC-146's ergodicity.
The nonsingular field also discharges the presupposition F_in ≪ lambda of main.tex:196 for every EGF with F_out ≪ lambda (EGF.IsEGFErgodic.inflowAC, through EGF.InflowAC.of_map_ac, C-6).

Instances of def:egf in DEC-146's form: the flows of every affine toroidal model and every isometry spherical model are EGFs iff the group of their moves is ergodic (EGF.AffineToroidalModel.isEGFErgodic_flow_iff, EGF.isEGFErgodic_torus_iff, EGF.IsometrySphericalModel.isEGFErgodic_flow_iff, EGF.isEGFErgodic_sphere_iff; the groups are definitionally torusAffineGroup and sphereRotGroup, EGF.egfGroup_torusAffineME, EGF.egfGroup_rotME); concrete inhabitants: the L2-model flows with the rotation of cosine 3/5 of S^1 (EGF.isEGFErgodic_sphere_two_witness), the rotation by sqrt 2 of R/Z (EGF.isEGFErgodic_circleRotFlow_sqrt_two; a rotation of the circle is an EGF iff of infinite order, EGF.isEGFErgodic_circleRotFlow_iff), the swap of two points (EGF.Swap.isEGFErgodic_flow).
questions: The Riemannian setting (main.tex:217) cannot be stated at the pin (no manifold volume). Reading taken, as the dispatch prescribes: (S, lambda) any measure space and the moves measurable equivalences preserving the lambda-null sets both ways, carried as the field 'nonsingular' of IsEGFErgodic, the property diffeomorphisms have for the volume (formalized on R^d with Haar measure, tori and spheres). With it the group form (the field 'ergodic') and C-26's generator form agree. The other design (no 'nonsingular' field and the generator form as the definition) is a strictly weaker predicate in general (it admits singular moves), which agrees on the paper's objects and agrees on the paper's objects; the author may prefer one of the two.

'for some policy alpha : S -> [0,1]^p': the policy is a parameter of the predicate (as in EGF.IsEGF), not existentially quantified, so that the theorems can name its weights; the existential form follows. Weights are not required positive, as printed; positivity (the softmax head of main.tex:288) is a hypothesis of the link to universality only (EGF.IsEGFErgodic.isKernelErgodic).

lambda is not assumed finite in the definition (a Riemannian volume need not be finite; the standing finite lambda of main.tex:161 is used only by the universality links, which assume [IsFiniteMeasure lam]).

corrections.notes: def:egf in DEC-146's form, sorry-free, standard axioms only; no hypothesis added to the corrected text beyond the abstraction of 'diffeomorphisms of a Riemannian manifold with its volume' as nonsingular measurable equivalences (C-6's property, automatic for diffeomorphisms; proved on R^d with Haar measure, tori, spheres). The corrected text's 'that is' is proved equivalent to the group form (EGF.isEGFErgodic_iff_symmDiff) and needs the nonsingularity (EGF.FourCycle.isGroupErgodic_not_forall). The optional witnesses of C-26's finding are proved in both directions (EGF.isEGF_not_isEGFErgodic with its instance EGF.isEGF_not_isEGFErgodic_sqrt_two; EGF.isEGFErgodic_not_isEGF), with the disclosed limits: the first measure is not the volume, the second not of full support; Furstenberg's smooth example is not formalized. For the master: switch C-26's anchor list to these names once the file graduates, then adopt under DEC-146 (added_hypotheses = []).
Carried: the field IsEGFErgodic.policy is EGF.IsEGFPolicy (alpha measurable, alpha^i ≥ 0, sum_i alpha^i = 1), C-27's corrected text.
Supporting only: the nonsingular field gives F_in ≪ lambda for every EGF with F_out ≪ lambda; C-6's anchors are unchanged.

kb_proposals: def:egf of record is EGF.IsEGFErgodic lam F Phi alpha (EGFScaffold.DefEGF, DEC-146): Phi : Fin p -> S ≃ᵐ S, fields policy (IsEGFPolicy, C-27), nonsingular (lam.map (Phi i) ≪ lam ∧ lam.map (Phi i).symm ≪ lam), ergodic (IsGroupErgodic lam (egfGroup Phi)). Use h.ergodic_moves for the generator form, h.isKernelErgodic hpos for the kernel, h.isUniversalPolicy / h.isUniversalFamilyEps for universality, h.inflowAC for F_in ≪ lambda. Torus and sphere moves as measurable equivalences: torusAffineME, rotME; their egfGroup is torusAffineGroup / sphereRotGroup by rfl.

Pitfall: ∆ (symmDiff, `open scoped symmDiff`) binds tighter than ⁻¹': `Φ ⁻¹' A ∆ A` parses as `Φ ⁻¹' (A ∆ A) = ∅`, a silently vacuous hypothesis; write `(Φ ⁻¹' A) ∆ A`. `measure_symmDiff_eq_zero_iff` needs `(μ := lam)` to unify through the OuterMeasureClass coercion.

A set a.e.-invariant under quasi-measure-preserving generators and inverses is a.e.-invariant under the generated subgroup of Equiv.Perm: EGF.ae_invariant_of_mem_closure_of_quasi (Subgroup.closure_induction carrying QMP of h and h⁻¹; Measure.QuasiMeasurePreserving.comp/.id/.preimage_ae_eq). Without nonsingularity the generator and group forms differ (EGF.FourCycle.isGroupErgodic_not_forall, Fin 4 with two atoms).

Forward (ℕ-)orbits of a rotation of infinite order of AddCircle T are dense: EGF.denseRange_nsmul_of_addOrderOf_eq_zero (Mathlib has only AddCircle.denseRange_zsmul_iff): -a ∈ closure by CompactSpace.tendsto_subseq and differences n_{j+1} - n_j - 1, then the closure is stable under (· - a) by image_closure_subset_closure_image. NoAtoms (volume : Measure (AddCircle T)) is not an instance at the pin: build it from AddCircle.volume_closedBall at ε = 0 with Metric.closedBall_zero.

A.e. statements for finite sums of Dirac masses reduce to the atoms: ae_add_measure_iff + ae_dirac_eq (MeasurableSingletonClass), then `decide` on Fin n after `show` of the concrete membership; every group is ergodic for a Dirac mass (EGF.isGroupErgodic_dirac). A finite measure with atoms on a ℤ-orbit: Measure.sum with weights 2⁻¹ ^ (Equiv.intEquivNat n), finiteness by Equiv.tsum_eq + ENNReal.tsum_geometric + ENNReal.one_sub_inv_two (EGF.orbitLam).
